candidates.attacker_control: YAML document content is fully attacker-controlled whenever a YAML configuration is loaded from an attacker-influenceable source (config file/URL/stream fetched from a third party, replaceable file, or path resolved through FileLocator/FileHandler). Tags and constructor arguments are parsed verbatim by Yaml.load(...).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Confirmed read methods are the real FileBasedConfiguration/InputStreamSupport load paths, not write-only helpers. Confirmed the LoaderOptions overloads do not mitigate: LoaderOptions configures parser/loader limits, not the object constructor, so `new Yaml(options)` remains unsafe. Acknowledged that configuration files are often trusted (reduces severity for many deployments) and that no in-repo test asserts safe parsing. Noted the orphaned test.yaml vs TestJSONConfiguration lines 42-52 as circumstantial evidence a YAML test was removed, not proof. Could not inspect the snakeyaml jar itself.
candidates.impact: Deserialization of attacker-influenced YAML into arbitrary object graphs: instantiation of attacker-selected classes with attacker-selected constructor arguments. Depending on classpath gadgets this can escalate to remote code execution and at minimum breaks the configuration parser's trust boundary and enables class-loading side effects/denial of service when configuration content is only partially trusted.
candidates.prerequisites: Application uses YAMLConfiguration (directly or as a FileBasedConfiguration via FileHandler/builders) and parses YAML from an untrusted-influenceable source; snakeyaml is on the classpath (declared optional in pom). Code-execution escalation additionally depends on gadget classes available on the application classpath; arbitrary-class instantiation and its side effects occur regardless.
candidates.root_cause: All YAML read entry points build SnakeYAML objects without restricting the object constructor: read(Reader)/read(InputStream) use `new Yaml()`; read(Reader, LoaderOptions)/read(InputStream, LoaderOptions) use `new Yaml(options)`, where LoaderOptions only carries parser limits, not a SafeConstructor. With the declared snakeyaml 1.25 dependency the default Yaml constructor resolves YAML type tags (e.g. `!!`) and constructs arbitrary classes with attacker-chosen arguments, rather than limiting parsing to plain scalars/maps/lists; the resulting objects are then loaded into the configuration hierarchy.
candidates.title: Unsafe YAML parsing in YAMLConfiguration (default SnakeYAML constructor allows arbitrary type instantiation)
candidates.trace: FileHandler.load(Reader/InputStream/URL) -> content.read(reader/stream) -> YAMLConfiguration.read(Reader) line 68 `new Yaml()` (and read(InputStream) line 120; read(..., LoaderOptions) lines 83 and 135) -> Yaml.load(in) resolves tags by loading/constructing referenced classes -> Map passed to AbstractYAMLBasedConfiguration.load(map) lines 74-78 and becomes the configuration hierarchy. FileHandler.load(Reader) lines 789-793 is the generic file-based entry point dispatching to the FileBasedConfiguration implementation.
candidates.unverified: SnakeYAML 1.25 internal constructor behaviour is not in this repository, so the arbitrary-instantiation claim rests on that library's known semantics. No runtime exploit, gadget chain, endpoint, or upstream fix commit/CVE mapping was verified; the removed-test inference is circumstantial.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data (unsafe polymorphic object construction during YAML parsing)

summary: Apache Commons Configuration 2.7-SNAPSHOT (early-2020 tree, snakeyaml 1.25). Strongest source-evidenced candidate: unsafe YAML parsing in YAMLConfiguration, which uses SnakeYAML's default (non-safe) constructor for every read path, allowing attacker-influenced YAML documents to instantiate arbitrary Java types (CWE-502, possible RCE via classpath gadgets). Snapshot-local supporting signal: src/test/resources/test.yaml exists but no YAML test class references it, while the parallel JSON fixture is consumed by TestJSONConfiguration. No runtime confirmation is claimed.
